page: Amazon Web Services x8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the x8i.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. The memory subsystem delivers top-tier cached read bandwidth, though Passmark memory scores and uncached large-block write bandwidth fall into the average and strong categories respectively. For database and key-value store workloads, the instance performs in the top tier, processing 171.86 million Redis SET operations per second and showing top-tier static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring external network-attached storage, and average single-core performance in stress-ng tests.

Given its massive DDR5 memory capacity and dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources, the x8i.24xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions enables top-tier prompt processing speeds for small and medium large language models, though text generation speeds remain average to strong. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-effective for large-scale in-memory databases, complex data compiling, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads that do not require local physical storage.
